_README: Zones for the island, cloned from a vanilla MTAreaVolume.
A zone is what makes people exist. MTZoneState is keyed by ZoneKey and
carries Server_Residents, NumResidents and BusTransportRate. Jeju ships
exactly seven volumes and Arini was inside none of them, so its bus stops
held 0 passengers no matter how long anyone waited.
world   = centre of the volume, WORLD coordinates.
scale   = RelativeScale3D on the brush, which is a unit box. This is the
volume the game tests against. Vanilla Gangjung uses
outline = HALF extent in uu of the rectangle drawn on the map. This is a
SEPARATE thing from the volume: TopViewLines is its own
world-space polygon, which is why a cloned zone kept drawing
Gangjung's shape over Arini no matter where the box went. Keep
it roughly consistent with scale by hand -- the relationship
between brush scale and world size has not been measured.
The zone registers and Arini appears in the resident system, but reports
0 residents. Residents likely need POIs to live at: MTResidentZoneState
carries a POIs array and MTZoneState a Server_Supermarkets one.
color = ZoneColor as [r, g, b, a], 0..1. Cloned from Gangjung it drew in
Gangjung's colour, which is the one thing that must not happen
when the point is telling two zones apart.

zones.name: Arini
zones._outline_points: Optional explicit polygon [[x,y], ...] in WORLD coords. Overrides `outline`. Vanilla zones are irregular and tile against each other, and the map label is drawn from this outline -- so shaping it is also how the label moves.
